README.md:3:## bitchat for Android
README.md:5:A decentralized peer-to-peer messaging app with dual transport architecture: local Bluetooth mesh networks for offline communication and internet-based Nostr protocol for global reach. No accounts, no phone numbers, no central servers.
README.md:7:This is the Android implementation of bitchat, fully protocol-compatible with the [iOS version](https://github.com/permissionlesstech/bitchat) for cross-platform mesh communication.
README.md:9:[bitchat.free](http://bitchat.free)
README.md:11:[GitHub Releases](https://github.com/permissionlesstech/bitchat-android/releases)
README.md:13:[<img alt="Get it on Google Play" height="60" src="https://play.google.com/intl/en_us/badges/static/images/badges/en_badge_web_generic.png"/>](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.bitchat.droid)
README.md:21:- **Dual Transport Architecture**: Bluetooth LE mesh for offline messaging, Nostr relays for internet-based messaging
README.md:22:- **Location-Based Channels**: Geographic chat rooms using geohash coordinates over Nostr relays
README.md:24:- **End-to-End Encryption**: [Noise Protocol](https://noiseprotocol.org) (XX pattern, X25519 + ChaCha20-Poly1305) for private messages over the mesh
README.md:26:- **Wi-Fi Aware Transport**: Higher-bandwidth local mesh on supported devices
README.md:31:- **Cross-Platform**: Binary protocol compatible with bitchat on iOS and macOS
README.md:38:- Noise Protocol sessions with forward secrecy; peer identities derived from static keys
README.md:41:- Foreground service keeps the mesh alive within Android background execution limits
README.md:43:### Nostr Protocol (Internet)
README.md:46:- Private messages fall back to Nostr for mutual favorites when the mesh is unavailable
README.md:53:- Core components: `MeshForegroundService` (persistent connectivity), `BluetoothMeshService` / `WifiAwareMeshService` (transports), `UnifiedMeshService` (transport selection), `NoiseSessionManager` (encryption sessions), `MessageRouter` (mesh/Nostr routing with outbox retry)

README.md:71:The app requests Bluetooth, location (required for BLE scanning), and notification permissions at runtime.

docs/05-audit/evidence/2026-07-29-initial-repository-audit/LEGAL-AND-README-CONTENT.txt:228:## bitchat for Android
docs/05-audit/evidence/2026-07-29-initial-repository-audit/LEGAL-AND-README-CONTENT.txt:230:A decentralized peer-to-peer messaging app with dual transport architecture: local Bluetooth mesh networks for offline communication and internet-based Nostr protocol for global reach. No accounts, no phone numbers, no central servers.
docs/05-audit/evidence/2026-07-29-initial-repository-audit/LEGAL-AND-README-CONTENT.txt:232:This is the Android implementation of bitchat, fully protocol-compatible with the [iOS version](https://github.com/permissionlesstech/bitchat) for cross-platform mesh communication.
docs/05-audit/evidence/2026-07-29-initial-repository-audit/LEGAL-AND-README-CONTENT.txt:234:[bitchat.free](http://bitchat.free)
docs/05-audit/evidence/2026-07-29-initial-repository-audit/LEGAL-AND-README-CONTENT.txt:236:[GitHub Releases](https://github.com/permissionlesstech/bitchat-android/releases)
docs/05-audit/evidence/2026-07-29-initial-repository-audit/LEGAL-AND-README-CONTENT.txt:238:[<img alt="Get it on Google Play" height="60" src="https://play.google.com/intl/en_us/badges/static/images/badges/en_badge_web_generic.png"/>](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.bitchat.droid)
docs/05-audit/evidence/2026-07-29-initial-repository-audit/LEGAL-AND-README-CONTENT.txt:246:- **Dual Transport Architecture**: Bluetooth LE mesh for offline messaging, Nostr relays for internet-based messaging
docs/05-audit/evidence/2026-07-29-initial-repository-audit/LEGAL-AND-README-CONTENT.txt:247:- **Location-Based Channels**: Geographic chat rooms using geohash coordinates over Nostr relays
docs/05-audit/evidence/2026-07-29-initial-repository-audit/LEGAL-AND-README-CONTENT.txt:249:- **End-to-End Encryption**: [Noise Protocol](https://noiseprotocol.org) (XX pattern, X25519 + ChaCha20-Poly1305) for private messages over the mesh
docs/05-audit/evidence/2026-07-29-initial-repository-audit/LEGAL-AND-README-CONTENT.txt:251:- **Wi-Fi Aware Transport**: Higher-bandwidth local mesh on supported devices
docs/05-audit/evidence/2026-07-29-initial-repository-audit/LEGAL-AND-README-CONTENT.txt:256:- **Cross-Platform**: Binary protocol compatible with bitchat on iOS and macOS
docs/05-audit/evidence/2026-07-29-initial-repository-audit/LEGAL-AND-README-CONTENT.txt:263:- Noise Protocol sessions with forward secrecy; peer identities derived from static keys
docs/05-audit/evidence/2026-07-29-initial-repository-audit/LEGAL-AND-README-CONTENT.txt:266:- Foreground service keeps the mesh alive within Android background execution limits
docs/05-audit/evidence/2026-07-29-initial-repository-audit/LEGAL-AND-README-CONTENT.txt:268:### Nostr Protocol (Internet)
docs/05-audit/evidence/2026-07-29-initial-repository-audit/LEGAL-AND-README-CONTENT.txt:271:- Private messages fall back to Nostr for mutual favorites when the mesh is unavailable
docs/05-audit/evidence/2026-07-29-initial-repository-audit/LEGAL-AND-README-CONTENT.txt:278:- Core components: `MeshForegroundService` (persistent connectivity), `BluetoothMeshService` / `WifiAwareMeshService` (transports), `UnifiedMeshService` (transport selection), `NoiseSessionManager` (encryption sessions), `MessageRouter` (mesh/Nostr routing with outbox retry)

docs/sync.md:3:This document specifies the gossip-based synchronization feature for BitChat, inspired by Plumtree. It ensures eventual consistency of public packets (ANNOUNCE and broadcast MESSAGE) across nodes via periodic sync requests containing a compact Golomb‑Coded Set (GCS) of recently seen packets.
docs/sync.md:7:- Each node maintains a rolling set of public BitChat packets it has seen recently:
docs/sync.md:16:This synchronization is strictly local (not relayed), ensuring only immediate neighbors participate and preventing wide-area flooding while converging content across the mesh.
docs/sync.md:25:Implementation: `com.bitchat.android.sync.PacketIdUtil`.
docs/sync.md:29:Implementation: `com.bitchat.android.sync.GCSFilter`.
docs/sync.md:54:- Header: normal BitChat header with TTL indicating “local-only” semantics. Implementations SHOULD set TTL=0 to prevent any relay; neighbors still receive the packet over the direct link-layer. For periodic sync, recipient is broadcast; for per-peer initial sync, recipient is the specific peer.
docs/sync.md:64:Encode/Decode implementation: `com.bitchat.android.model.RequestSyncPacket`.
docs/GeohashPresenceSpec.md:5:The Geohash Presence feature provides a mechanism to track online participants in geohash-based location channels. It uses a dedicated ephemeral Nostr event kind to broadcast "heartbeats," ensuring accurate and privacy-preserving online counts.
docs/GeohashPresenceSpec.md:7:## Nostr Protocol
docs/GeohashPresenceSpec.md:52:Clients must update their Nostr filters to listen for both chat and presence events on geohash channels.

docs/security-review-jul-27.md:1:# Bitchat Android — Security Review
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:3:**Commit:** 92d07b22 (worktree: `~/.opencode/worktrees/bitchat-security-review`)
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:5:**Method:** Read-only static review of `crypto/`, `noise/`, `identity/`, `mesh/`, `protocol/`, `net/`, `service/`, `nostr/`, `geohash/`, `ui/`, `features/`, manifest & build config. All findings verified against source.
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:11:### C1. Noise session key material (DH shared secrets, chaining keys) written to logcat — ships in release
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:15:### C2. Remote decompression bomb — pre-auth memory exhaustion via ~30-byte BLE write
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:17:For compressed v2 packets the decoder reads a 4-byte attacker-controlled `originalSize` and immediately does `ByteArray(originalSize)` — up to 2 GiB per packet. The ratio guard is skipped when `compressedSize == 0` and is 50,000:1 anyway (real deflate max ≈ 1032:1). Runs inline on the GATT callback path; any nearby unauthenticated BLE peer can OOM/crash the foreground service with tiny writes.
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:23:### H1. Replay-window bit shift direction is wrong — Noise transport replay protection broken
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:24:`noise/NoiseSession.kt:69-106`
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:25:Bit indexing is LSB-first, but the window-shift code right-shifts the byte string. A replayed captured frame (nonce 0) tests a zero bit and is accepted; only the single most-recent nonce is reliably blocked. A passive BLE observer can replay DMs, ACKs, and receipts.
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:27:### H2. Announcement signing key not bound to Noise key — "first announce wins" peer-ID impersonation
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:28:`mesh/AnnouncementIdentityValidator.kt:13-36`, `mesh/SecurityManager.kt:282-313`, `mesh/MessageHandler.kt:265-299`
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:29:An attacker can replay a victim's Noise public key (→ victim's peerID) inside an announcement signed with the *attacker's* Ed25519 key. On fresh installs or for never-authenticated peers the forged binding wins, and the genuine victim's later announce is rejected as "key replacement".
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:32:`mesh/MessageHandler.kt:88` (also 125; `nostr/NostrProtocol.kt:277`)
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:37:Decrypted DM bodies (mesh + Nostr) are posted with full text in `BigTextStyle`/`InboxStyle`; no `VISIBILITY_SECRET` / lockscreen visibility set. Content renders on lock screen and to any notification-listener app; no opt-out.
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:39:### H5. No signature verification on incoming public Nostr events — relay can forge any user
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:40:`nostr/GeohashMessageHandler.kt:44-105`, `nostr/LocationNotesManager.kt:358-414`, `nostr/NostrRelayManager.kt:663-706`
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:41:`NostrEvent.isValidSignature()` (exists, `NostrEvent.kt:171`) is never called for kind 20000/20001/1. A malicious/compromised relay (auto-selected from a daily third-party list, see M9) can inject events with arbitrary pubkeys — impersonating any user in any geohash channel, spoofing participants, caching attacker-chosen nicknames, registering DM aliases.
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:43:### H6. Automatic delivery/read receipts over Nostr = online-presence & location oracle
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:44:`nostr/NostrDirectMessageHandler.kt:134-138,165-175`, `nostr/NostrTransport.kt:316-384`
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:52:`nostr/NostrIdentity.kt:137-177`, `ui/GeohashViewModel.kt:184-193`
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:53:Geohash identity = HMAC(deviceSeed, geohash), never rotated. A passive observer of a channel can recognize returning users months later and assemble their full history in that channel; the plaintext `["n", nickname]` tag (`nostr/NostrProtocol.kt:167-169`) links the same person across channels.
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:56:`mesh/PacketProcessor.kt:43-95`, `mesh/BluetoothPacketBroadcaster.kt:122-124`
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:59:### H10. Unauthenticated packet types relayed mesh-wide with attacker-controlled TTL — flood/amplification
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:60:`mesh/SecurityManager.kt:268-280`, `mesh/PacketRelayManager.kt:59-107,134-163`
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:61:Signature verification enforced only for ANNOUNCE/MESSAGE/FILE_TRANSFER/LEAVE. FRAGMENT, REQUEST_SYNC, NOISE_* verify unconditionally and are relayed (unconditionally at TTL ≥ 4) with no rate limit. One BLE radio can make the entire mesh re-broadcast forged traffic, draining bandwidth and battery.
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:64:`mesh/BluetoothMeshService.kt:671-676`, `sync/GossipSyncManager.kt:168-199`
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:67:### H12. ANNOUNCE replay with TTL=7 forces Noise session teardown + fake "direct neighbor"
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:68:`mesh/SecurityManager.kt:78-90`, `mesh/BluetoothMeshService.kt:586-621`
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:69:Duplicate ANNOUNCEs are re-accepted at TTL ≥ 7; direct-link is inferred from TTL alone (excluded from the signature, attacker-settable). Replaying a victim's recent ANNOUNCE at TTL=7 repeatedly tears down the victim's Noise sessions, breaking in-flight DMs.
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:75:### M1. No low-order point / all-zero DH rejection — Noise spec violation, key-compromise downgrade
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:80:`noise/NoiseSessionManager.kt:228-252,312-316`
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:83:### M3. Stable 8-byte peerID in BLE scan response — passive long-term tracking
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:84:`mesh/BluetoothGattServerManager.kt:400-412`, `mesh/BluetoothMeshService.kt:54`
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:85:The scan response embeds the truncated fingerprint of the *persistent* static Noise identity, surviving restarts and MAC rotation (by design, for dedup). Any passive sniffer can track a user across time/place. Nickname is broadcast in every ANNOUNCE; ANNOUNCE gossip TLVs disclose the user's neighbor graph.
docs/security-review-jul-27.md:88:`mesh/FragmentManager.kt:32,202-263`
